subject: English
title: Arun and Maya Find Opposite Words
hook: Explore the fun world of opposites with Arun and Maya!

slides.title: Hot and Cold are Opposites
slides.storyContext: Arun touches hot tea and says 'Hot!' Maya drinks cold water and says 'Cold!' They're opposite!

points.label: Opposites
points.text: Words that mean completely different things

slides.inSimpleWords: Hot and cold are opposite words!

image.alt: Hot and Cold are Opposites — Opposites

slides.title: Big and Small
slides.storyContext: Maya shows a big watermelon and a small grape. 'Big and small are opposites!',she says.

points.label: Big ↔ Small
points.text: These words mean completely opposite sizes

slides.inSimpleWords: Big and small are opposite size words!

image.alt: Big and Small — Opposites

slides.title: Happy and Sad
slides.storyContext: Arun laughs and feels happy. But when he loses his toy, he feels sad!

points.label: Happy ↔ Sad
points.text: These are opposite feelings

slides.inSimpleWords: Happy and sad are opposite feelings!

image.alt: Happy and Sad — Opposites

slides.title: Fast and Slow
slides.storyContext: Arun runs very fast! Maya walks very slowly. They move opposite ways!

points.label: Fast ↔ Slow
points.text: These words mean opposite speeds

slides.inSimpleWords: Fast and slow are opposite speed words!

image.alt: Fast and Slow — Opposites

slides.title: Light and Dark, Day and Night
slides.storyContext: When the sun rises, it's light and day. When it sets, it's dark and night!

points.label: Light ↔ Dark
points.text: Opposite brightness

points.label: Day ↔ Night
points.text: Opposite times

slides.inSimpleWords: Light and dark, day and night are opposites!

image.alt: Light and Dark, Day and Night — Opposites

slides.title: More Opposite Pairs
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya play an opposites matching game!

example.problem: Find opposite words: tall, clean, old, young, wet
example.solution: short, dirty, new, old (pair), dry — opposites found!

slides.inSimpleWords: Different words can mean complete opposites!

image.alt: More Opposite Pairs — Opposites

slides.title: More Opposite Words
slides.storyContext: Arun says: open/closed, loud/quiet, left/right, up/down!

points.label: Position opposites
points.text: left/right, up/down, in/out

points.label: Action opposites
points.text: open/close, start/stop

slides.inSimpleWords: Positions and actions have opposite words too!

image.alt: More Opposite Words — Opposites

slides.title: Opposites Everywhere
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write their favorite opposite pairs on the wall!

points.label: Feeling opposites
points.text: happy/sad, brave/scared

points.label: Description opposites
points.text: big/small, hot/cold

points.label: Action opposites
points.text: fast/slow, start/stop

slides.inSimpleWords: Opposite words mean completely different things!

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Rhyme Time
hook: Discover the magic of words that sound the same at the end!

slides.title: What Are Rhyming Words?
slides.storyContext: Arun sings 'cat' and Maya sings 'bat'. They sound the same at the end!

points.label: Rhymes
points.text: Words that sound the same at the end

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyming words sound the same at the end!

image.alt: What Are Rhyming Words? — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Cat, Hat, Bat, Rat
slides.storyContext: Arun lists words: cat, hat, bat, rat. They all rhyme because they end the same way!

points.label: 'at' rhyme family
points.text: cat, hat, bat, rat, mat, fat, sat

slides.inSimpleWords: Cat, hat, bat all rhyme together nicely!

image.alt: Cat, Hat, Bat, Rat — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Dog, Fog, Log, Hog
slides.storyContext: Maya shows: dog, fog, log, hog. All end with 'og' sound!

points.label: 'og' rhyme family
points.text: dog, fog, log, hog, bog, clog

slides.inSimpleWords: Dog, fog, log rhyme with the 'og' sound!

image.alt: Dog, Fog, Log, Hog — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Sun, Run, Fun, Bun
slides.storyContext: Arun jumps and shouts: 'Rhyming is fun! I like to run and eat a bun!'

points.label: 'un' rhyme family
points.text: sun, run, fun, bun, gun, nun, stun

slides.inSimpleWords: Sun, run, fun rhyme with the 'un' sound!

image.alt: Sun, Run, Fun, Bun — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Make Rhyming Pairs
slides.storyContext: Maya teaches: take a word and find another word that rhymes with it!

points.label: Finding rhymes
points.text: Listen to the last sounds and match them

slides.inSimpleWords: Find words that end with the same sound!

image.alt: Make Rhyming Pairs — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Creating Rhyming Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya make a rhyming sentence together!

example.problem: Make a rhyming sentence with 'cat' and 'hat'.
example.solution: 'The cat wore a hat.' Cat and hat rhyme!

slides.inSimpleWords: Use rhyming words to make fun sentences!

image.alt: Creating Rhyming Sentences — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Rhyming Words in Poems
slides.storyContext: Maya recites: 'Roses are red, violets are blue.' The words rhyme and sound beautiful!

points.label: Poems
points.text: Poems often use rhyming words to sound pretty

slides.inSimpleWords: Poems use rhyming words to sound nice!

image.alt: Rhyming Words in Poems — Rhyming Words

slides.title: Rhyming Words Everywhere
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write their own rhyming poem together!

points.label: Definition
points.text: Rhyming words sound the same at the end

points.label: Rhyme families
points.text: cat/hat, dog/fog, sun/fun, rat/bat

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyming words sound alike and make poems fun!

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Noun and Pronoun Journey
hook: Learn how nouns name things and pronouns replace them!

slides.title: What is a Noun?
slides.storyContext: Arun points: 'Look! A dog, a tree, a house! These are all nouns — they name things!'

points.label: Noun
points.text: A word that names a person, place, animal, or thing

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns are words that name people, places, things!

image.alt: What is a Noun? — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Nouns Name People
slides.storyContext: Maya lists: 'Arun, teacher, doctor, mother — these are nouns for people!'

points.label: Person nouns
points.text: boy, girl, teacher, doctor, mother, farmer, police

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns that name people are person words!

image.alt: Nouns Name People — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Nouns Name Places
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'Delhi, school, park, temple — these are places. All nouns!'

points.label: Place nouns
points.text: city, school, park, temple, library, garden, beach

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns that name places are place words!

image.alt: Nouns Name Places — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Nouns Name Animals and Things
slides.storyContext: Maya points to things: 'Dog, cat, book, pencil, chair — all nouns!'

points.label: Animal and thing nouns
points.text: dog, cat, bird, book, pencil, chair, table, toy

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name animals and objects too!

image.alt: Nouns Name Animals and Things — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: What is a Pronoun?
slides.storyContext: Arun says: 'Instead of saying Arun every time, I say I or me. That's a pronoun!'

points.label: Pronoun
points.text: A word that replaces a noun

slides.inSimpleWords: Pronouns replace nouns in sentences!

image.alt: What is a Pronoun? — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: I, You, He, She, It, We, They
slides.storyContext: Maya teaches the main pronouns: 'I am Maya. You are my friend. He is Arun. She/It/We/They too!'

points.label: Personal pronouns
points.text: I, you, he, she, it, we, they

slides.inSimpleWords: I, you, he, she, it, we, they are pronouns!

image.alt: I, You, He, She, It, We, They — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Using Pronouns Instead of Nouns
slides.storyContext: Arun shows how to replace nouns with pronouns!

example.problem: Maya likes books. Maya reads books. Maya writes about books.
example.solution: Maya likes books. She reads them. She writes about them. (She replaces Maya, them replaces books)

slides.inSimpleWords: Use pronouns to avoid repeating the noun!

image.alt: Using Pronouns Instead of Nouns — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: My, Your, His, Her, Our, Their
slides.storyContext: Maya says: 'This is my pencil. That is your book. This is his toy. That's her doll.'

points.label: Possessive pronouns
points.text: my, your, his, her, its, our, their

slides.inSimpleWords: Possessive pronouns show who owns something!

image.alt: My, Your, His, Her, Our, Their — Nouns and Pronouns

slides.title: Nouns and Pronouns
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya create a chart showing nouns and their pronoun replacements!

points.label: Nouns
points.text: Name people, places, animals, things

points.label: Pronouns
points.text: I, you, he, she, it, we, they (replace nouns)

points.label: Possessives
points.text: my, your, his, her, our, their (show who owns)

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name. Pronouns replace. Both are important!

image.alt: Nouns and Pronouns — Nouns and Pronouns
